title: Editing paragraph with errors (six errors)
subject: English
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 57 (Editing paragraph with errors (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 57: Grammar and vocabulary retrieval masterclass. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Paragraph with errors
paras: resilience is when you keep going even when things are hard, it is something we all need. My brothers friend failed his test twice but he definately did not give up he kept practising every evening. Now there going to the library together every week.

blocks.answers: Corrected: Resilience (capital) ... are hard. It is (comma splice) ... My brother's (apostrophe) friend ... definitely (spelling) ... give up. He kept (missing full stop) ... Now they're (their / there / they're) going to the library together every week.

blocks.title: Sort into: Means hope or strength / Means people and belonging
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Means hope or strength, Means people and belonging.
blocks.answer: Means hope or strength: resilience; legacy; perseverance. Means people and belonging: heritage; diversity; community

model.title: Edit: 'resilience is when you keep going, it is important, we should all try.'

parts.text: Fix the comma splice with a full stop

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Resilience means keeping going when life is hard. We rise, we rest, we climb again.

keywords.def: words used in an imaginative, not literal, way
ambitious words used across many subjects, such as resilience or legacy

questions.q: Correct the comma splice: 'The stair was broken, she kept climbing.'
questions.a: The stair was broken, but she kept climbing. (or a full stop / semi-colon)

questions.q: Use 'legacy' in a sentence about someone you admire
questions.a: For example: 'My grandfather's legacy is the patience he taught us.'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a paragraph titled 'What belonging means to me', using a metaphor, a deliberate pronoun shift, parallelism and a colon. Starter: 'Belonging is...'
questions.a: A paragraph with four devices used accurately and labelled.

questions.q: Extend: edit the error paragraph on the sheet (six errors)
questions.a: Six errors corrected: capitals, comma splice, apostrophe, spelling of 'definitely', missing full stop, 'their/there'.

questions.q: Stretch: rewrite one sentence of your paragraph to make it more concise
questions.a: A tighter sentence with the same meaning.

options: We keep three things, hope: courage and patience.
We keep: three things hope courage, and patience.
We keep three things: hope, courage and patience.
questions.a: C) We keep three things: hope, courage and patience.. A colon introduces the list after a complete clause.

questions.q: A comma splice joins two sentences with...
Answer the ponder: which tool will you keep, and why?
